Recipe (JSON):
  canvas {"w","h"} 16..1024 REQUIRED; frames 1..32 = 8; fps 1..60 = 12; loop bool = false; still_t 0..1 = 0.5 (time shown when frames=1); origin [x,y] = canvas centre (default x/y of layers); ramps {"main": preset|["#rrggbb" dark->light, 2-12]} REQUIRED, more names allowed; outline {"mode": "none"|"dark"|"black"|"selective"|"custom", "color"} = dark; dither 0..0.3 = 0 (no dithering anywhere, the default: keep it 0 unless the user asks for dithering or a style that uses it; above 0 = dithered colour steps, dithered soft edges (fade) and dithered fade-outs (dissolve, particle fade_in/out)); tones 2..12 = 12 (at most this many colours from every ramp, evenly picked: the style's colour count); detail 0..1 = 1 (noise texture everywhere: 0 = calm, flat blobs; 1 = as the layers say); shading level|interior|lit = level (how every shape's colour bands sit inside it: level = by the shape's own brightness; interior = darker towards each shape's edge, a rounded body; lit = lit from shade_angle, the near side light and the far side dark, like a ball in sunlight; the silhouette never changes); shade_angle -360..360 = -135 (where the light comes FROM, degrees: -90 = above, -135 = above-left); shade_depth 1..32 = 6 (px: how deep the bands reach in); seed 0..999999 = 1; impact {"frames": [1-3 frame numbers, 0-based], "mode": "invert"|"silhouette"|"flash"} = none (anime hit frames: on those frames every visible pixel, sprite included, is inverted, or the main ramp's darkest or lightest colour; one frame at the moment of the hit, for a punchy anime or fighting-game hit); camera {"tilt": 0.05..1 = 1, "lean": -1..1 = 0, "height": 0.05..1 = 1} (see Camera above); mirror "none"|"x" = none (x flips the effect left-right, positions included; the sprite keeps its pixels); paths {"name": {"x": anim, "y": anim}} (motion paths on the effect's whole t; a layer with "along": "name" takes its x/y from it); subject {"x","y","align": "center"|"feet"} or omit (where the user's sprite goes), plus optional frames/fps (an animated sprite's strip: filled in for you), dx/dy (animated whole-pixel offsets), shake (animated px of seeded jitter), life [a, b] (shown only while t is inside it), dissolve (animated 0..1, takes it away: gone halfway, or dithered away when the recipe dither is above 0) and tint {"colour": "#rrggbb", "amount": animated 0..1} (the whole sprite mixed toward the colour in quarter steps, after lights; its dark outline stays below 1, 1 = a flat silhouette; sliders bind subject.tint.amount), wave {"amp": px, "length": 16, "cycles": 1, "axis": "x"|"y", "flow": [0, 0], "only": ["#rrggbb", ...]} (the sprite's OWN pixels move: each row slides sideways (axis x; y = each column up and down) by amp px along a wave length px from crest to crest, cycles whole waves per loop; flow = whole times the picture scrolls round per loop; everything wraps inside the sprite, so a seamless tile stays seamless; only = the colours that move, the rest stays put, and near = 0..255 RGB distance (default 48) within which other shades count as one of them; whole pixels, never resampled), shore {"water": ["#rrggbb", ...], "near": 48, "foam": "#ffffff", "film": "#rrggbb", "width": 6, "reach": 3, "lines": 2, "cycles": 1, "thickness": 1.5, "ragged": 0.3} (waves washing up the coast of the sprite's own water, which the engine finds from the water colours: each wave a foam line starting width px out to sea, rolling in and washing reach px up the land, leaving film (a wet colour, e.g. a darker sand) where it went, then thinning away; lines waves at once, cycles per loop, ragged = how broken the foam line is), echo {"count": 3, "gap": 1, "offset": [dx, dy], "colour": "#rrggbb", "amount": 0.75, "fade": "tint"|"flicker"|"dither"} (afterimages: count copies of the sprite as it was gap frames per copy earlier, its place, animation frame and shake then, each pushed offset px further, drawn behind it oldest first; colour tints them, the oldest by amount; fade flicker = they blink every other frame, dither only when the user asks for dithering); its animated values run on the effect's t; layers [...] REQUIRED (may be [] when subject.wave, shore or echo makes the sprite the effect); controls [...]; name, notes strings.
  Ramp presets: arcane, blood, electric, fire, frost, holy, nature, poison, shadow, smoke, water.
Time: loop -> t = i/frames; one-shot -> t = i/(frames-1). A layer's life [a, b] limits it to that part of t; inside, its animated values run on local time u = 0..1.
Animated value: a number, {"from": a, "to": b, "ease": linear|in|out|in_out|in_cubic|out_cubic|step, "start": 0, "end": 1}, {"keys": [[u, v], ...], "ease": ...}, {"wave": {"mid", "amp", "cycles": 1, "phase": 0}}, or a formula {"expr": "40 + 10*sin(tau*u)", "scale": 1, "offset": 0} (expr of u, times scale plus offset; division by 0 and anything not a number give 0; sliders bind .offset / .scale or mul it).
Layer fields common to every type: id (a-z0-9_, unique) REQUIRED, type REQUIRED, z back|front = "back"; plane screen|ground|upright = "screen"; enabled bool = true; ramp str = "main"; intensity number|animated = 1.0; dissolve number|animated = 0.0; breakup edge|blocks|scan = "edge"; life [a, b] in 0..1 = [0.0, 1.0]; lo num 0.0..0.95 = 0.12; fade num 0.0..0.9 = 0.0; seed int 0..999999 = 0; group str = ""; phase num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; cycle bool = false; ride str = "". Fields of one z sharing a ramp merge into one shape (max) and are painted once; each keeps its own lo/fade (fade = a dithered soft edge, drawn only when the recipe dither is above 0). intensity 0..1 picks the ramp colour; dissolve 0..1 fades the layer away (dithered away when the recipe dither is above 0, else as its breakup says: edge = wears away from its edges inward, blocks = falls apart in 2x2 chunks, scan = wiped away top-down). phase = where a looping layer starts in its cycle (copies of one loop out of step); cycle = the layer loops inside its life window even in a one-shot effect; ride = a path name: the layer is CARRIED by that path (its own x/y plus how far the path has travelled since t = 0), unlike along, which puts it ON the path. Layers placed by add_part carry an "rng" pair that keeps their random look: copy it along unchanged.
Layer types:
- glow: soft or hard radial light (cores, auras, flashes, pools of light); angle turns a squashed glow (an oval) clockwise in degrees. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; shape soft|linear|hard = "soft"; angle num -360.0..360.0 = 0.0; outline bool = true
- ring: an ellipse outline; width = solid core px, soft = fade px (shockwaves, circle rims, halos with width 0). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; width number|animated = 1.0; soft number|animated = 3.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- rays: spikes radiating from a point between inner and inner+length (bursts, starbursts, crackle); spin = the direction of ray 0 in degrees (0 = right, -90 = up); tip_fade = how much each ray darkens toward its tip (0 = bright all the way: glints, light spikes). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; count int 1..64 = 12; length number|animated = REQUIRED; inner number|animated = 0.0; width number|animated = 3.0; jitter num 0.0..1.0 = 0.3; alternate num 0.0..0.95 = 0.4; tip_fade num 0.0..1.0 = 0.55; spin number|animated = 0.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- bolt: jagged lightning from start to end with branches; progress grows it, flicker re-rolls its shape every N frames; plane ground lays it on the floor (cracks: it is pressed flat by camera.tilt, its lines keep their width). start [x, y] = REQUIRED; end [x, y] = REQUIRED; segments int 2..32 = 10; jag num 0.0..0.6 = 0.12; branches int 0..8 = 2; branch_length num 0.05..1.0 = 0.35; width number|animated = 1.0; soft number|animated = 3.0; progress number|animated = 1.0; flicker int 0..32 = 0; outline bool = true
- arc: a crescent along a circle from `start` degrees sweeping `sweep` degrees (slashes, swooshes); 0 deg = right, 90 = down. profile "slash" = a swing that WHIPS (sword, axe, claw hits): it draws itself over the layer's life, the head easing out across the whole sweep in the first `head` of it while the tail chases from `tail` on, thickest just behind a tapered tip (`taper` px), the leading rim brightest, the tail crumbling in chunks; keep sweep constant (the motion is built in) and time it with life. claws = that many strokes side by side `spacing` px apart, each a beat later (claw marks). points (profile slash only) = the swing along a path instead of a circle: [[x, y], ...] 2-24 points relative to x/y (radius / start / sweep not needed); corners smooth = a curve through them (S-swings, hooks, a weapon's real arc), sharp = straight lines between them (zigzags, frantic cuts); it travels from the first point to the last; flip = the other edge glows. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; start number|animated = 0.0; sweep number|animated = REQUIRED; thickness number|animated = 6.0; soft number|animated = 2.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; profile crescent|taper|slash = "crescent"; trail num 0.0..1.0 = 0.5; head num 0.05..1.0 = 0.45; tail num 0.0..0.95 = 0.3; taper num 0.0..64.0 = 6.0; claws int 1..5 = 1; spacing num 0.0..32.0 = 4.0; points [[x, y], ...] 2..24 points relative to x/y = none; corners smooth|sharp = "smooth"; flip bool = false; outline bool = true
- star: star polygon lines {points/step} (hexagram = 6/2, pentagram = 5/2); rotation = where the first point is, in degrees (0 = right, -90 = up). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; points int 3..24 = 6; step int 1..11 = 2; rotation number|animated = 0.0; width number|animated = 0.6; soft number|animated = 2.5; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- glyphs: pixel rune letters placed around a circle (rune bands on magic circles); rotation = where the first rune sits, in degrees (0 = right, -90 = top). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; count int 1..48 = 8; size number|animated 0.0..64.0 = 6.0; rotation number|animated = 0.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; level int -12..11 = -1; thickness int 1..4 = 1; outline bool = false
- particles: many small things that move: sparks, motes, drops, debris, or your own pixel sprite. mode burst: out from (x, y) travelling `speed` px along `direction` +- spread/2 degrees (-90 = up), slowing down; travel: the same but at constant speed and from the whole emitter (wind, jets, sprays, a flow, sideways streams); rise/fall: from a disc of `radius`, travelling `speed` px up/down (wobble = sideways sway px; drift = px sideways over its life: slanted rain, smoke bending in the wind); orbit: round a circle of `radius`; twinkle: fixed spots in a disc of `radius`, pulsing; converge: born on a ring `radius` out and pulled in to (x, y), faster as they near (charge-ups, energy gathering, a vacuum). source sprite / edge = born on the user's sprite's pixels / its outline instead (disintegrating, burning outlines, a teleport out; with converge, energy drawn out of the sprite into (x, y)). vortex = turns about (x, y) over a particle's life (swirls, tornado debris); drag 0..1 = travel slows down; floor = px below (x, y) where particles land (debris, drops), bounce 0..1 = how far they bounce back. line > 0 emits along a line `line` px long through (x, y) at line_angle degrees (0 = horizontal) instead of the disc (a row of jets, rain from a cloud's flat base, a wall of flame). spacing even = evenly spaced instead of random (round an orbit, and in time: births, a loop's ages); together = every particle born at the start (a burst that shows on its first frame). Loops: each particle cycles `cycles` times per loop; one-shots: each lives `lifespan` of the layer's time. gravity = px pulled down (+) by the end of a particle's life. shape: sparkle (pixel star), dot (round blob: embers, bubbles, motes), droplet (teardrop pointing along its motion: rain, drips, tears), streak (line along its motion, longer when faster: rain, speed lines, flying sparks), chunk (tumbling shard lit from the top-left: rocks, debris, ice shards, crumbs), custom (your sprite in `pixels`, drawn 1:1: hearts, notes, coins, leaves, any small symbol). size [min, max] px = sparkle arm / dot and droplet diameter / chunk length / streak minimum length; with shrink > 0 a particle shrinks and vanishes below 1 px, so use shrink 0 for custom sprites and chunks that should stay whole; shrink < 0 grows it (-1 = twice the size by the end; a custom sprite never scales). intensity below 1 draws the particles that many ramp steps darker. pixel_ramp = how many ramp colours a custom sprite's digits were written for: then its digits keep their place on a longer or shorter ramp (the top digit stays the lightest). emit: follow (particles move with x/y) or trail (each is born where x/y was at its birth and stays there: a trail behind a moving thing, so give it the SAME x/y path as the thing, or better: put both on one path with along). Per particle: fade_in / fade_out = the share of its life it takes to come in / go out (each particle appears and vanishes whole, in turn; dithered in and out when the recipe dither is above 0); blink = how many times it blinks over its life (fireflies, glints), blink_duty = the share of each blink it is visible; orient = a custom sprite drawn facing RIGHT turns (mirrors or quarter-turns, never resampled) to face where it moves; depth auto = an orbit's near half (below its centre) is drawn in front of the subject and the far half behind (things circling AROUND a sprite). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; mode burst|rise|orbit|twinkle|fall|travel|converge = "burst"; count int 0..256 = 16; radius number|animated = 4.0; speed number|animated = 24.0; direction num -360.0..360.0 = -90.0; spread num 0.0..360.0 = 360.0; gravity num -200.0..200.0 = 0.0; size [min, max] whole = [1, 3]; shrink num -2.0..1.0 = 1.0; cycles int 1..8 = 1; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; wobble num 0.0..16.0 = 0.0; lifespan num 0.05..1.0 = 0.6; shape sparkle|dot|droplet|streak|chunk|custom = "sparkle"; pixels ["row", ...] ('.' clear, '1'-'9' ramp colour) = none; emit follow|trail = "follow"; fade_in num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; fade_out num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; blink num 0.0..16.0 = 0.0; blink_duty num 0.05..0.95 = 0.5; depth flat|auto = "flat"; orient bool = false; spacing random|even = "random"; together bool = false; drift num -512.0..512.0 = 0.0; line num 0.0..512.0 = 0.0; line_angle num -360.0..360.0 = 0.0; pixel_ramp int 0..12 = 0; outline bool = false; source area|sprite|edge = "area"; vortex num -8.0..8.0 = 0.0; drag num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; floor num 0.0..512.0 = 0.0; bounce num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0
- ribbon: a tapered strip trailing along a path (comet tails, homing shots, a wand's swish, a dragon's ribbon of flame): along = the path (required), length = how much of the effect's time it trails behind (0.25 = a quarter), width px at the head, taper 0..1 = how much it narrows toward the tail (1 = to a point), brightest along its middle and at the head. Put the projectile itself (a glow, an image) on the same path. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; length num 0.02..1.0 = 0.25; width number|animated = 6.0; taper num 0.0..1.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- beam: light column or spike standing on (x, y) going up `height`; upright (and not turned) it is a solid the camera sees: a round footprint `width` px across, flattened by the tilt, swept up (and up-left in oblique views); taper 0 = a cylinder (a pillar of light), 1 = a cone (an ice spike, a crystal); brightest on its axis, soft blurs its edge (a glow); top_fade 0..1 fades it toward its far end (a beam from the sky, a pillar dissolving upward); angle turns it clockwise about (x, y) in degrees (90 = pointing right: a laser, a jet of light) and a turned beam is a flat strip. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; width number|animated = 8.0; height number|animated = REQUIRED; soft number|animated = 3.0; taper num 0.0..1.0 = 0.3; top_fade num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; angle num -360.0..360.0 = 0.0; outline bool = true
- noise: value-noise volume clipped to a disc or a column (fire masses, smoke, gas, churning portal cores; for candles, torches and campfires prefer flame). erosion 0 = solid shape, ~0.5 ragged edges, 1+ breaks apart; scale = noise blob size in px; scroll = px the pattern moves over the layer's life (negative y = upward, like flames); column stands on (x, y): upright (and not turned) it is a flame with a body the camera sees, burning on a round patch `width` px across (flattened by the tilt) and rising up (up-left in oblique views); angle turns the whole volume clockwise about (x, y) in degrees (90 = a column pointing right: a flame jet, a gust). x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; shape disc|column = "disc"; radius number|animated = 16.0; width number|animated = 16.0; height number|animated = 32.0; scale num 1.0..64.0 = 6.0; octaves int 1..5 = 3; erosion number|animated = 0.5; scroll [x, y] = [0.0, -16.0]; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; angle num -360.0..360.0 = 0.0; outline bool = true
- spiral: `arms` curling out from (x, y) to `radius` (vortices, whirlpools, drains, swirling portals, galaxies). turns = how many times an arm winds (negative winds the other way); width = solid arm px, soft = fade px; spin = rotation in degrees (+ clockwise; for a seamless loop change it by a multiple of 360/arms); brightest at the centre, fading over the outer quarter. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; radius number|animated = REQUIRED; arms int 1..12 = 3; turns num -4.0..4.0 = 1.5; width number|animated = 1.5; soft number|animated = 2.0; spin number|animated = 0.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- image: a sprite pasted exactly as drawn, never outlined or recoloured: one of the user's own pictures (image = its name, "projectile"; frames/fps = an animated strip) or YOUR OWN drawing in pixels (one frame of rows, or a list of frames played at fps; '.' clear, '1'-'9' the layer's ramp, 1 darkest, 'a'-'z' colours you name in colours): a snake's head, a summoned sword, a skull, a ghost, a rune, a coin, anything up to 64x64 px; draw its outline yourself (it gets none). It sits centred on (x, y) or follows a path (along) / rides one (ride). facing travel turns it the way it moves in mirrors and quarter turns (faces = where it points as drawn); spin = whole turns over its life, a quarter at a time; count/stagger = a volley of copies stagger of the effect apart. The throw tool builds one from the user's picture with its path, trail and impact. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; image str = "projectile"; pixels ["row", ...] or [["row", ...], ...] frames, up to 64x64 and 16 frames ('.' clear, '1'-'9' ramp colour, 'a'-'z' from colours) = none; colours {"a": "#rrggbb", ...} = none; faces right|left|up|down = "right"; facing travel|none = "travel"; spin num -16.0..16.0 = 0.0; count int 1..8 = 1; stagger num 0.0..0.5 = 0.08; frames int 1..32 = 1; fps int 1..60 = 12
- shape: a free-form shape YOU draw, for anything no other layer is (a sword of light, a ghostly hand, wings, a crescent, a snake's body, streams of light round a beam, waves on water). points are px relative to (x, y): one outline [[x, y], ...], several (one inside another is a hole), {"keys": [[u, outlines], ...], "ease"} morphing between outlines with the same point counts (wings flapping, a hand closing), or {"curves": [{"x": formula, "y": formula, "z": formula, "n": 48, "base": y}]}: n points from formulas of s (0..1 along the curve) and u (the layer's time), redrawn every frame (a wave rolling, a helix turning, a tentacle swaying); base closes a curve straight down to that y (the water under a wave line, a hill). closed false = lines `width` px wide instead of filled outlines (streams, whips, runes, cracks, wind lines): taper narrows them toward their end, reveal 0..1 draws them on from the start. depth auto = each part goes behind the sprite (and under the other back layers) where its z formula is below 0 and in front where it is 0 or more: things circling AROUND something (a beam, the sprite). smooth 0..1 rounds corners into curves; scale, rotation (degrees clockwise) and squash move the points (it is redrawn, never resampled). fill: edge (light inside, dark rim, bevel px deep; a line: light along its middle), linear (dark to light toward fill_angle), radial (light at x/y), flat (one colour band, level 0..1). Filled with matter instead: smoke (a lit smoke texture, its edge broken by the noise; keeps small holes such as a skull's eyes; grain = blob px, erosion 0..2 = how ragged the edge, billow = lumps, flow [x, y] = px the texture drifts per loop, bevel = px to the full body), puffs (soft round billows) or cartoon (drawn cartoon puffs: lit top, dark underside, a crease where one overlaps another; they bring their own light and dissolve puff by puff), fire (the shape burns, tongues up to `reach` px rise off its top, holes stay open; flow [0, -40] makes them rise; tongues_only = only the tongues). smoke and fire fill closed outlines; puffs and cartoon also string along lines (width = puff size, spacing, roll = whole turns round the line per loop, drift = px along per loop, taper; they grow with scale) and fill closed outlines (grain = puff size). source "sprite" (no points) = the shape is the user's sprite's silhouette, `lift` px higher: fill it with smoke, puffs, cartoon or fire. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; points [[x, y], ...] | [outline, ...] | {"keys": [[u, outlines], ...], "ease"} | {"curves": [{"x": formula, "y": formula, "z": formula, "n": 32, "base": y}]} REQUIRED; source points|sprite = "points"; lift number|animated = 0.0; closed bool = true; smooth num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; scale number|animated 0.0..64.0 = 1.0; rotation number|animated = 0.0; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; fill edge|linear|radial|flat|smoke|puffs|cartoon|fire = "edge"; fill_angle num -360.0..360.0 = -90.0; bevel num 0.5..64.0 = 3.0; level num 0.0..1.0 = 0.7; grain num 1.0..32.0 = 4.0; octaves int 1..5 = 3; erosion num 0.0..2.0 = 0.35; billow num 0.0..2.0 = 0.8; flow [x, y] = [0.0, 0.0]; drift num -512.0..512.0 = 0.0; roll num -8.0..8.0 = 1.0; spacing num 0.3..4.0 = 1.0; highlight num 0.0..1.0 = 0.6; crease bool = true; reach num 0.0..64.0 = 14.0; tongues_only bool = false; width number|animated 0.0..128.0 = 3.0; taper num 0.0..1.0 = 0.0; reveal number|animated 0.0..1.0 = 1.0; depth flat|auto = "flat"; outline bool = true
- flame: drawn fire: teardrop tongues standing on (x, y), wide low and pointed at the tip, hot in the root's middle and dark at the edges (reads drawn, not noisy). Candles (1 small tongue, sway 0.1, flicker 0.2), torches (2-3 tongues), campfires and bonfires (3-5, spread ~1), cartoon flame tongues (1 wide tongue, curl 0.6+), fire walls (7 tongues, or a row of flame layers). width/height = the main tongue in px; tongues 1..7 (the others alternate left and right, smaller); spread = how far apart; taper 0..1 = how much shorter the outer tongues are (1 a campfire's peak, 0 a level wall); base 0.1..1 = how wide the root is; sway = the tip swinging, curl = the tip whipping (both grow with height, the root stays put); flicker = ragged edges running up; chips = bits breaking off the outer shell; core = how much of it is the hottest colour; cycles = flickers per loop (whole numbers keep a loop seamless); angle turns it (90 = a jet pointing right). plane upright so it leans with an oblique camera. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; width number|animated = 12.0; height number|animated = 24.0; tongues int 1..7 = 1; spread num 0.0..2.0 = 1.0; taper num 0.0..1.0 = 1.0; base num 0.1..1.0 = 0.6; sway num 0.0..1.0 = 0.25; curl num 0.0..1.0 = 0.3; flicker num 0.0..1.0 = 0.5; chips num 0.0..1.0 = 0.3; core num 0.5..3.0 = 0.9; cycles int 1..6 = 1; angle num -360.0..360.0 = 0.0; outline bool = true
- puffs: round masses summed into one shape with nested colour bands, for cartoon smoke, poofs, dust clouds and fiery cartoon explosions (reads drawn, not noisy). mode burst: a hot flash, then masses thrown out (`throw` 0..1), slowing, growing, cooling and rising (`rise`), breaking up late (`thin`); poof: smoke thrown out in a cone toward `direction` (degrees, -90 = up) `spread` wide, rising and burning out; column: a looping stream of puffs born at (x, y) rising `height` px along `direction` (chimney smoke, steam, a smoking crater); cloud: a looping clump wobbling in place, lighter on top. radius = body size px, count = masses (more = lumpier), lump = how lobed each mass is, billow 0..1 = small puffs round each mass, highlight 0..1 = how lit from above each mass is (0 = flat masses). Colour comes from each mass's heat: use a fire ramp for explosions, a grey or tinted ramp for smoke and dust. x number|animated = origin; y number|animated = origin; along str = ""; mode burst|poof|column|cloud = "burst"; radius number|animated = 20.0; count int 1..24 = 7; throw num 0.0..1.0 = 0.6; rise num 0.0..3.0 = 0.4; height number|animated = 40.0; spread num 0.0..3.2 = 1.2; direction num -360.0..360.0 = -90.0; lump num 0.0..3.0 = 1.0; billow num 0.0..1.0 = 1.0; highlight num 0.0..1.0 = 0.6; thin num 0.0..1.0 = 0.3; squash num 0.1..4.0 = 1.0; outline bool = true
- light: lights the SUBJECT (the user's sprite): it recolours the sprite's own pixels in pixel-art steps and draws nothing else, so it needs a subject.   A slider writes value*scale+offset into every bound path (mode set, the default). Paths: layers.<id>.<field>, into animated values (layers.ring.radius.to, layers.fx.intensity.keys.2.1, layers.aura.radius.wave.mid), subject.<field>, ramps.<name> (ramp control, value = a preset name or colour list), camera.tilt, outline.mode, dither, tones, detail, seed. mode mul multiplies the WHOLE bound value (a number or every number of an animation: from/to, every key, a wave's mid and amp) by value*scale+offset, so an animated field keeps its animation and gets a size slider (a 0.5..1.5 slider = half to one and a half); mode add adds it instead. Toggles bind layers.<id>.enabled. Controls override the values they bind. The user drags them anywhere, so every position must stay valid (both slider ends inside the bound field's range), and one control sets each value. Any layer may carry a "group" name (layers that belong together; remove_group removes them). A layer may name a preset ramp it did not declare ("ramp": "frost").

Rules that save a failed render:
- Only the fields in the reference exist; anything else is an error. Colours come only from ramps: there is no colour field on a layer.
- Canvas pixels from the top-left; y grows DOWN. Every angle is in degrees: 0 = right, 90 = down, -90 = up (directions, spins, rotations, arcs, lights).
- Every layer needs a unique id and a type, plus its REQUIRED fields. Layers without x/y sit on origin (default: canvas centre).
- A slider binds plain numbers: inside an animated value bind .to / .from / .keys.<i>.1 / .wave.mid.
- If the effect is cut off at the edges or floats in a lot of empty space, render(fit_canvas=true) resizes the canvas around it (everything moves; the reply tells you by how much).
- When an error says "did you mean", use that name.
- Sliders win: a value a control writes always renders as the control says. Patching such a value moves that control (the reply tells you); to animate a slider-driven value, bind it with "mode": "mul" so the slider scales the whole animation.
- The reply lists every layer's frames and peak frame and names the layer behind each warning. Frames come cropped to what the effect draws (the reply says where the crop sits on the canvas) at 2x; render(zoom=N, frames=[...]) looks closer at chosen frames. get_preset(name, peek=true) shows a preset without replacing your working recipe.
- A recipe that places no subject does not draw the user's sprite: add "subject" when they gave you one.
